# Source and local changes

- Klepton `https://github.com/shinyquagsire23/Klepton`, revision `1fe7e6caf6bb8bc90c1a5e61d5b9bfc6e110fa32`, MIT, copyright Max Thomas; its license is `LICENSE`. Only two pinned upstream files were retrieved, not a complete source archive: `upstream/kl_openxr.c` SHA-256 `223e361f5b3f629e27248131cd955ae5ae2b9f370a4e4f81d783b6f4242ff2b3` and `upstream/kl_openxr.h` SHA-256 `1f2d6a3f78f9ddcf64597a32aaffb2bb922d131fcdabdaaf9e0a5b35259df26c`. License SHA-256 `8705e40805c9267df365b89ceaa34a56498e34b7d3b6ebb95e9c12a7d3827a2b`.
- `src/core.c` is a selective adaptation, not the whole upstream file. `klxr_two_call` is taken from upstream lines 1056–1069 (names map to Khronos errors). `klxr_CreateInstance` follows lines 1262–1302 with zero advertised extensions, host configuration gate and bounded non-reused handles replacing the singleton. `klxr_GetSystem` follows lines 1327–1342, with actual host availability instead of unconditional presence. Dispatch adapts lines 718–739 and 6613–6753; unknown entries return errors rather than upstream's aborting stubs. Normal builds refuse session support; a partial test-only Metal resource/session slice is described below. Production session, action state and tracked input are not implemented. This inventory records local transformations in lieu of a patch directly applicable to the full upstream file. Instance/system properties follow upstream lines 1310–1391 but identify the actual partial runtime and take all device, limits, and tracking fields from a host callback rather than synthetic Quest defaults. Path interning and reverse lookup adapt upstream lines 3284–3318, with per-instance ownership, stale-ID protection, and full path-grammar validation added. Action-set bookkeeping adapts lines 3260–3274 and 3320–3359 with owner, unique-name and stale-handle checks. The Metal resource/session slice adds local code behind test-only `KL_NATIVE_TEST_METAL_PARTIAL`; production withholds the extension. Typed refusal functions are generated from official Khronos prototypes to avoid ABI-mismatched abort stubs. Local `core.c` SHA-256 `0954fbad3448f0f59d1355d7a0e5c32fafd4aff6ac9054dc7753db0f688b15fa`; refusal functions `70036549faaec37341dfc2834931c2caf5982ecc0d1b61465ec324a5c3f41a9b` and dispatch `76a4ea21274295e8f52230eb4adc250f580861b6fac84897443dd237ed7b4aed`.
- Khronos `openxr.h` and `openxr_platform_defines.h` were copied from the already-local `openxr-sys` 0.13.1 Cargo package's bundled `OpenXR-SDK/include/openxr`. Its lockfile package checksum is `4b8d66081de28c2fa40216182a37292fe38aeea20bc184612504d5e64daf5359`; crate VCS metadata gives openxrs repository commit `f50cf13afc047f96d540d9d85a08e023e0d3647d` (not an independently established OpenXR-SDK commit). Header declares API 1.1.54. Header SHA-256 respectively `d8bc0c759dbecfbd29901418f809d919f2d1ab6c710ab5fdf5205766fb92910b` and `59a5369c34013beeea505aa0465768acad558ac016bab3320780e2a653a07bfb`. Headers say Apache-2.0 OR MIT; the bundled OpenXR-SDK Apache license is retained in `OPENXR-SDK-LICENSE`, SHA-256 `cfc7749b96f63bd31c3c42b5c471bf756814053e847c10f3eb003417bc523d30`. Their Khronos copyright notices remain in the files.

- `openxr_platform.h` from the same `openxr-sys` package is retained for official Metal extension structures; SHA-256 `0da6b2ca34132704366236cebb9112dee85ae802c529476b902ecf4dcea278fd`. The retained Khronos Apache license and in-file alternative SPDX notice also apply.

- Session state adapts the upstream event/session lifecycle with an explicit host-driven state machine and acknowledged begin/end; it replaces synthetic READY with real host event callbacks and preserves running state on failed drain. Host adapter remains unimplemented.

- Swapchain acquire/wait/release ordering adapts Klepton FIFO behavior but delegates availability and write completion to a new explicit native host boundary. Timeout/failure preserves ownership, and destroy refuses acquired images. The table is not connected to a real host in this component.
- `src/pose_math.c` extracts quaternion/pose composition and relative-transform algebra from upstream `kl_openxr.c` lines 2405–2460, with new finite/unit-quaternion validation. SHA-256 `841bcc2b80e86435c25e81fe7d4138da49746cde86433eec9f8d27a63aa4dbdc`; it is linked into the provider for mock-tested reference-space transforms.

- View configuration enumeration follows upstream but gets separate recommended/max dimensions, sample counts and stereo/opaque support from explicit native host metadata; it never derives recommendations from maximums or invents a frame/pose.

The partial test lifecycle adds an optional host `request_exit` acknowledgment and explicit host `EXITING` event. Host STOPPING and EXITING represent actual logical session transitions; neither is inferred. The provider requires a successful request and completed drain before accepting EXITING. Session header SHA-256 `7ff099735cb5774fe3fff8f0dade323870e30def322ab393b55e54352e7454c5`.

Pose action create/destroy bookkeeping adapts pinned upstream `kl_openxr.c` lines 3361–3384. Native changes add type restriction, name and owner/path validation, bounded non-reused handles, duplicate detection and child invalidation; POSE_INPUT and BOOLEAN_INPUT with left/right hand subaction paths are accepted. It does not implement action spaces, attachment, synchronization, tracked controller state or pose query.

The partial reference-space implementation accepts the standard XrSpaceVelocity output chain used by openxrs; no velocity samples are available, so the returned velocity flags are zero. Unsupported output chains remain refused.

- Action identity bookkeeping accepts the five OpenXR legacy action types (pose, boolean, float, vector2 and vibration), with stale handle and unsupported-type tests. Binding, action state and haptic operations still refuse; identity does not assert active devices or input.

- Native input host v1 (`include/input_host.h`, SHA-256 `55b83899218d26681045f3f10d0130ea197bb2e80534af509b11b2e49406fd9a`) and attach/sync support explicit host-observed disconnected hands only. Same-ID/time polls are accepted; rewinds and inconsistent IDs fail, as do connected hands until real profile and state mapping is implemented. Other unsupported bindings and haptics still refuse. The macOS ARM64 UBSan `tests/metal_mock.c` covers attach order, repeated and conflicting samples, failed sampling, and connected-hand refusal; this is a host mock without headset or game.

- The four non-extension profiles used by xrizer legacy setup accept validated, instance-owned suggested bindings, which do not activate a profile. Attached actions return inactive Boolean, Float, Vector2f or Pose state only after a successful disconnected host sample; failed sync invalidates the sample and state queries fail closed. Connected devices remain unsupported. Owned boot and UBSan mock tests pass, including path/type rejection and stale-state refusal. Injected-host diagnostic vMt8Z7 observed all four actual xrizer suggestions and attach succeed, but sync returned XR_SESSION_NOT_FOCUSED; actual focused state and tracking remain unverified.

- `tests/xrizer_pose_probe.m` and `test-xrizer-pose-probe.sh` are an owned native-host diagnostic. The runner records and removes three guards only in a sealed snapshot; it is never an accepted runtime configuration. With injected focused lifecycle, disconnected input and changing tracked head samples, snapshot 2AhwXe passed four actual native xrizer calls including invalid tracking, role/state and pose-array controls and clean cancellation. It does not prove a Windows guest, real input/tracking, headset, or game. Snapshot manifest SHA-256 `2db388d73b855d1985d8b2dea838b68b9edb54a75d898340b59789cc118133ac`; changed-source record `e336bad843c8d2037406541845a8f96ab56272ffbe800c2a67d48971418765bf`; log `4d59d0fbf58e3a7081fa1e9a4940090dce1de7c67b67fda5bf5b0d5a2629fdeb`.

- Final-source owned-apple-test snapshot aZWPby makes no compositor edits: manifest `3b16d9f8bafb0ffaea077329415855eb24adb8ceff758bae5f3cf7ee78297110`, fixture-only substitution record `3fdbb0f4aabb60a8de53559da494be97b9b8e467d9a5f8fb9aba35d8bca00e7e`, dylib `89fcbe65fdb6862b8a21a6bef68b6acdf8f47adec92d067c283b31707287a78c`, log `76668681475c20c705bd6434ae2e588709b5c308b25885eead0190e160b3dcad`, execution environment `acfb543bf33e966812b082f52abcc1229b5d6f722598afc7519cd25c8e68937a`. The test still injects host focus, tracking and disconnected hands and makes no physical or Windows guest claim.

- Expanded final-source owned snapshot Un4dP4 passed disconnected controller-with-pose/haptic and System device-pose array/null controls in addition to the earlier four-frame test. Manifest `6fbe011294d1367849693e214675e16ecfc00b01b82eae9d7084df72b9840ff0`, native dylib `5853797da60b4f46d5734f7c799df79e7bc3526e84bddc2aeebac4fa94aaa567`, log `92c3db2ef9d9923772bd8f4267f36be4226021422c526cb3f320e56df88e6d5a`; macOS ARM64, injected host, not a guest or physical test.
